text: The author's motive to illuminate the complexities of patriotism and the costs of war is structurally embedded in the narrative through the characters' navigation of moral dilemmas and the consequences of political decisions. By drawing on his own experiences as a war correspondent, Leo Franklin uses the political thriller genre to force readers to confront the human and ethical toll of conflict, thereby linking the thematic exploration of patriotism directly to the personal and societal costs depicted in the plot.
